extra_misconceptions.fact: Microwaves and radio waves are nonionizing radiation with photon energies too low to eject electrons from atoms.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Microwave ovens and cell phones emit ionizing radiation that strips electrons directly from human DNA.

extra_misconceptions.fact: ALARA keeps exposure as low as reasonably achievable using time, distance, and shielding while accounting for background dose.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The ALARA principle guarantees zero radiation exposure during nuclear science experiments and lab visits.

extra_misconceptions.fact: External gamma or X-ray irradiation passes through matter without leaving radioactive contamination on your body or gear.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Exposure to gamma rays from a sealed check source makes your clothing and skin permanently radioactive.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The radiation symbol marks any area, container, or device where ionizing radiation sources or X-ray equipment are present.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The yellow and magenta trefoil symbol warns only against lethal nuclear weapons and reactor meltdowns.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to an atom's orbital electrons when struck by ionizing radiation versus visible light?
Why does doubling your distance from a point source cut your radiation exposure rate to one-fourth?
Where must the magenta or black three-bladed radiation trefoil symbol be posted in a laboratory?
Which three physical factors do you control under the ALARA principle to minimize your total dose?

extra_misconceptions.fact: All isotopes of an element share the exact same proton count and chemical identity, differing only in neutron number.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Isotopes of the same chemical element have different numbers of protons and occupy different periodic table boxes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Protons and neutrons are composite hadrons built from three valence up and down quarks bound by strong-force gluons.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Protons and neutrons are indivisible elementary particles just like orbital electrons.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Both gamma rays and X-rays are massless electromagnetic photons; gamma rays originate in the nucleus and X-rays in electron shells.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Gamma rays and X-rays are made of heavy charged particles ejected from the outer electron shells.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most light elements have stable isotopes with balanced neutron-to-proton ratios that never undergo spontaneous decay.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every isotope of a natural element on the periodic table is unstable and undergoes radioactive decay.

extra_socratic_questions: What changes inside the nucleus across three isotopes of carbon while the atomic number stays at six?
Which combinations of up and down quarks form a positively charged proton versus a neutral neutron?
What distinguishes the origin of a gamma ray from an X-ray if both are high-energy photons?
Under what neutron-to-proton ratio condition does an atomic nucleus become unstable and decay?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Magnetic fields only steer and focus the particle beam in a circle, while alternating electric fields add kinetic energy.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Static magnetic fields in a circular accelerator increase the speed and kinetic energy of charged particles.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Relativistic particles approach the speed of light asymptotically, gaining momentum and relativistic energy rather than exceeding c.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Particle accelerators can push protons and electrons well past the speed of light in a vacuum.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Gas molecules scatter and stop the particle beam, so accelerator tubes require an ultra-high vacuum cleaner than outer space.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Air inside an accelerator beam tube helps cool the particles as they travel around the ring.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hospitals and industry use compact linear accelerators and cyclotrons daily to treat cancer and produce medical radioisotopes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Linear accelerators and cyclotrons are used exclusively for high-energy theoretical quark research.

extra_socratic_questions: What role do oscillating radio-frequency electric fields play versus superconducting dipole magnets?
Why must the beam pipe inside a synchrotron or linear accelerator be pumped down to an ultra-high vacuum?
What happens to the magnetic field strength in a synchrotron as accelerated protons gain relativistic energy?
Which detector measurements allow physicists to reconstruct short-lived particles created in a collision?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ionizing radiation creates positive and negative air ions that neutralize the static electric charge stored on the foil leaves.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Radiation discharges a foil electroscope by physically blowing the metal leaves together with particle wind.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cloud chamber tracks are tiny droplets of alcohol condensing along the trail of ions left behind by passing charged particles.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The white trails inside a cloud chamber are the subatomic alpha and beta particles glowing in the dark.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Backscattered alpha particles proved that almost all atomic mass and positive charge sit in a tiny, dense central nucleus.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rutherford's gold foil experiment proved that positive charge is spread evenly throughout a solid atom.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouts BSA safety rules require a qualified adult to handle, store, and position all radioactive sources during experiments.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scouts may freely carry unsealed radioactive sources in their pockets to test homemade electroscopes.

extra_socratic_questions: Why do the charged foil leaves of an electroscope collapse when an ionizing source is held nearby?
What visual differences distinguish thick alpha tracks from thin, erratic beta tracks in a cloud chamber?
Why does a cloud chamber require a layer of supersaturated alcohol vapor cooled over dry ice?
Who is required to handle and position the radioactive check source during your Merit Badge experiments?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Every functional survey meter registers natural background radiation from cosmic rays and terrestrial radionuclides in soil and rock.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Geiger counter clicking in an empty room with no check sources nearby indicates a broken detector tube.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Paper stops heavy, doubly charged alpha particles, whereas beta particles require plastic or aluminum and gamma rays require lead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A single sheet of notebook paper shields a survey meter probe against beta particles and gamma rays.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Point-source radiation intensity obeys the inverse-square law, so tripling your distance drops the net count rate to one-ninth.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Moving three times farther from a small gamma check source reduces the measured count rate by one-third.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thinner air at high altitudes provides less atmospheric shielding, resulting in higher cosmic radiation doses on mountains and flights.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Natural background radiation is identical at sea level, on a high mountain peak, and inside a commercial jet.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement must you record with your Geiger counter before bringing any test source near the probe?
Why does a thin sheet of paper stop alpha particles completely while gamma rays pass right through it?
What happens to the net counts per minute when you move the detector probe from two centimeters to six?
Why does indoor radon gas pose a long-term health hazard when it seeps into an unventilated basement?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Reactor fuel is enriched to only three to five percent uranium-235, which makes a nuclear weapons detonation physically impossible.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A commercial nuclear power plant can detonate like an atomic bomb if the cooling water pumps fail.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The moderator slows fast neutrons down to thermal speeds so they are more likely to cause fission in uranium-235 nuclei.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The moderator in a pressurized water reactor absorbs extra neutrons to shut down the chain reaction.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fission heat boils water into high-pressure steam that spins a mechanical turbine coupled to an electromagnetic generator.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Nuclear reactors convert ionizing gamma radiation directly into alternating current inside the reactor vessel.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cooling towers emit only clean, nonradioactive water vapor from the secondary condenser loop to reject waste thermal heat.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The tall hyperboloid cooling towers at a nuclear station release clouds of radioactive smoke into the sky.

extra_socratic_questions: What role do the ping-pong balls and mousetraps represent in a nuclear fission chain reaction model?
Why must a thermal reactor use a water or graphite moderator to slow down freshly emitted fission neutrons?
What happens to the reactor power level when boron or cadmium control rods are lowered into the fuel core?
Which energy conversions transform the kinetic energy of fission fragments into electrical power on the grid?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Medical imaging tracers use isotopes with half-lives of hours so activity decays quickly after the diagnostic scan finishes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Diagnostic nuclear medicine uses radioisotopes with thousand-year half-lives so doctors have weeks to scan.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Irradiation passes gamma rays or electron beams through sealed food to kill bacteria and pests without making the food radioactive.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Food irradiation sterilizes produce and spices by mixing radioactive dust into the packaging.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Spacecraft RTGs contain no moving parts or fission chain reactions; thermocouples convert natural plutonium-238 decay heat into electricity.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Deep-space radioisotope thermoelectric generators use a miniature nuclear fission reactor with control rods.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Carbon-14 has a 5,730-year half-life, limiting radiocarbon dating to organic remains younger than roughly 50,000 years.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Carbon-14 radiocarbon dating accurately measures the age of billion-year-old volcanic rocks and dinosaurs.

extra_socratic_questions: Why do physicians choose short-lived gamma emitters like technetium-99m for diagnostic medical imaging?
What property of americium-241 alpha emissions enables a household ionization smoke detector to sense fire?
Why do deep-space probes bound for the outer planets rely on plutonium-238 radioisotope thermoelectric generators?
Which targeting techniques allow radiation therapy beams to destroy a deep tumor while sparing healthy tissue?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Nuclear careers span associate-degree radiation technicians, bachelor-level reactor engineers, and hospital imaging technologists.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every career in nuclear science requires a doctoral degree in theoretical physics and works at a weapon lab.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Strict shielding and dosimetry controls keep average nuclear plant worker doses lower than those of flight crews and interventional staff.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Nuclear power plant workers routinely receive higher annual radiation doses than medical staff or airline crews.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Reactor operators must complete years of plant-specific training and pass rigorous Nuclear Regulatory Commission licensing exams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any licensed mechanical engineer can operate the control room of a commercial nuclear power station.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Health physicists are radiation safety scientists who monitor dosimetry, design shielding, and enforce regulatory exposure limits.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Health physicists are medical doctors who perform surgery on patients in hospital emergency rooms.

extra_socratic_questions: What daily safety responsibilities distinguish a plant health physicist from a licensed reactor operator?
Why must a commercial nuclear reactor operator pass federal NRC licensing exams and simulator drills?
Which clinical certifications and degree paths are required to work as a hospital medical physicist?
What personal dosimetry devices must nuclear facility workers wear and log during every shift?
